claims.text: Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance that leads to pesting during high-temperature air exposure.
The proposed intervention is cold-spraying an approximately 50 μm metallic aluminum layer onto the as-cast alloy.
The aluminum-coated alloy is to be diffusion-annealed at 750 °C for 1 hour in an inert atmosphere.
The treatment will produce a graded aluminum-enriched surface region.
Aluminum will diffuse slightly into the substrate during the 750 °C anneal.
Diffusion annealing will create a coherent graded interface between the aluminum-rich layer and the substrate.
During exposure to air at 800 °C, the aluminum-enriched surface will oxidize preferentially to form alumina.
The resulting alumina scale will be dense, continuous, protective, and adherent.
The alumina scale will limit oxygen diffusion into the bulk alloy.
The treatment will significantly reduce oxygen uptake during a 5-hour exposure to air at 800 °C relative to untreated material.
The treatment will suppress or prevent pesting during a 5-hour exposure to air at 800 °C.
Minimal alteration of the alloy core will preserve room-temperature tensile ductility.
Minimal alteration of the alloy core will preserve high-temperature yield strength.
Optimized cold-spray and annealing parameters are expected to produce an alumina scale stable under thermal cycling.
The claimed oxidation-protection boundary is approximately 5 hours in air at 800 °C.
The claimed mechanical-performance boundary includes room-temperature ductility and yield strength at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹.
